newsitem.title: UK: British ex-hostages pray for captives in Kashmir.
newsitem.headline: British ex-hostages pray for captives in Kashmir.

text.p: Two Britons who were held hostage in Beirut led a prayer vigil on Sunday for four Western tourists kidnapped by Islamic militants in Kashmir 18 months ago.

The vigil coincided with an Indian newspaper report that the four men -- Britons Keith Mangan and Paul Wells, American Donald Hutchings and German Dirk Hasert -- had been killed last December by their captors.

Terry Waite, a former emissary of the Archbishop of Canterbury, and John McCarthy, who were both held hostage in Beirut, appealed for information at a special church service near Wells's home town of Blackburn in northern England.
"Myself and John McCarthy would like to say this -- anyone who has any information whatsoever about the Western hostages, please now come forward and let us know.
"Even if that news is not good news please let us have the information," said Waite, who was kidnapped in Beirut in January 1987 and held captive for nearly five years.
Earlier, the Indian Express newspaper reported from New Delhi that a jailed member of the Kashmiri militant group that kidnapped the Westerners had told interrogators they were killed last December.
Waite said he would continue to live in hope until there was proof that the hostages, who were captured while trekking in Kashmir, were dead.

McCarthy added: "It is terribly important that they might hear something over the radio that we are all hoping and praying for them. It keeps people going. We must maintain hope. They will be hoping we are doing that."
Wells's father, Paul, appealed to the men's captors to let their families know whether they were dead or alive.
"If they are dead, as some of the rumours say, we need to know so we can bring them home and give them a proper burial," he said.
